text:
cheng: Heads up — forecasting a notable shift toward long-context streaming in EU and APAC for the first week of next month. Need a short preheat + cost plan. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
leah: How big is the shift? rough numbers pls (tokens/hr, % streaming)
mike: Are we sure this is regional or global? marketing event in EU or an app change?
cheng: It's regional-first (EU), tied to a partner rollout — expected average context growth from 1k -> 8k tokens and streaming sessions rising from 12% -> ~48% of requests. Rough projected peak: 3.2B tokens/hr EU region for a 6h window.
alina: Oof. That will blow through current warmpool latency targets. Do we have warm GPU preheat windows in EU?
cheng: We have a 2-hr preheat currently on eu-prod, but given KV cache cold-starts with 8k context we should increase to 4-6h for steady-state. Quick calc: to keep p95 latency under 250ms we need ~18 reserved GPUs for the 6h peak.
dennis: Can you paste the calc?
cheng: Sure — here's the back-of-envelope:
```
assumptions:
  avg_tokens_per_stream: 6_000
  streaming_ratio: 0.48
  reqs_per_hour: 200k
  tokens_per_hour = reqs_per_hour * avg_tokens_per_stream = 1.2B
  peak_factor: 2.7 -> 3.24B tokens/hr
gpu_throughput_tokens_per_hour = 200M  # for our optimized kernel profile @ 100 contextavg
required_gpu_hours_per_hr = ceil(3.24B / 200M) = 17 -> round to 18 nodes
preheat_duration = 6h -> 18 nodes * 6h = 108 GPU-hours of reserved preheat
```
leah: thx. That matches my model roughly. Cost delta? (eu g4 equiv pricing used in cost sheet)
mike: If we use burst instead of full reserved for first 2h, we can reduce reserved commitment but risk higher p95. Tradeoff: cost vs SLO.
alina: Also network peering: if APAC spikes, cross-region fallback will add RTT and might push more requests to eu nodes -> need routing cap. Can we set routing policy to prefer local until 85% util then spill to dedicated fallback in us-west?
dennis: I ran a quick cost estimate: at $3.2 / GPU-hour (reserved rate) -> 108 GPU-hours = $345.6 for the preheat window. If we instead spin on-demand taxable GPUs at $9 / GPU-hour for burst (6h) -> 18*6*9 = $972. So significant.
cheng: Good call — also quantization gains: if we drop to int8 variant for streaming sessions we get ~1.6x throughput but need to validate quality. That could drop required nodes to ~11, lowering cost ~35-40%.
aleina: @cheng can you run a small AB on int8 for the partner dataset? 1h experiment is enough to check hallucination/regression.
cheng: On it. I'll schedule 2 nodes for a 90-minute test and share eval metrics.
oncall-bot: incident-check: no open incidents in eu-prod. Warmpool preheat job queued (id=wp-197245)
mike: For rollout plan — propose: day -2 enable canary int8 for 1% of traffic in eu, day -1 scale preheat to 50% reserved (9 nodes) + 9 burstable, day0 scale to 100% reserved if int8 checks out. Fallback policy -> route to us-west dedicated pool at 80% util.
dennis: I'll update the cost forecast sheet with both scenarios (full reserved vs hybrid burst + int8).
aleina: Thanks all. Cheng please paste the AB results and we'll lock preheat by EOD Friday. :thumbsup:
